req.title: Show index page
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET / with an HTML page listing all posts ordered by created descending.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates GET / returns HTTP 200 with an HTML page listing all posts ordered by created DESC. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — normal GET / with seeded data returns 200 and shows the known post title; (2) negative NEG — wrong HTTP method (POST /) returns 405, not 200; (3) boundary BVA — empty database (zero posts) still returns 200 with valid HTML but no post titles; (4) DT — two posts exist and ordering is verified (most-recent first); (5) STC — response Content-Type is text/html confirming HTML delivery. Mutation resilience: exact status codes, exact byte strings, exact ordering assertions, both sides of the 200/non-200 boundary tested.

tests.name: test_index_returns_200_and_shows_seeded_post_title
preconditions: Database is initialised with fixture data (1 post: 'test title' by user 'test')
actions: Send GET / via Flask test client
trace: R-FLASKR-001: HTTP 200; HTML with post titles
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'test title' in r.data
assert 'text/html' in r.content_type

tests.name: test_index_empty_database_returns_200_no_post_titles
preconditions: Database is initialised with schema but NO post rows (zero posts boundary)
actions: Send GET / via Flask test client against empty posts table
expected: Response body does NOT contain b'test title'
trace: R-FLASKR-001: HTTP 200; HTML page even when post list is empty (zero-item boundary)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    # Remove all posts to reach zero-post boundary
    get_db().execute('DELETE FROM post')
    get_db().commit()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'test title' not in r.data
assert 'text/html' in r.content_type

tests.name: test_index_posts_ordered_by_created_descending
preconditions: Database is initialised with fixture data (1 existing post created 2018-01-01)
A second post with a later created timestamp is inserted
actions: Insert a newer post directly into the database
Send GET / via Flask test client
expected: Response body contains both post titles
The newer post title appears before the older post title in the response body
trace: R-FLASKR-001: posts ordered by created descending
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    db = get_db()
    db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO post (title, body, author_id, created) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
        ('newer title', 'newer body', 1, '2024-06-01 12:00:00')
    )
    db.commit()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'newer title' in r.data
assert b'test title' in r.data
newer_pos = r.data.find(b'newer title')
older_pos = r.data.find(b'test title')
assert newer_pos < older_pos
assert newer_pos != -1
assert older_pos != -1

from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    count = get_db().execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post').fetchone()[0]
    assert count == 1

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'test title' in r.data
